units.title: Me and my family

words.def: your mum, a woman in your family
words.ex: My dad is my father, and my mum is my ___.

words.def: your dad, a man in your family
words.ex: My mum is my mother, and my dad is my ___.

words.def: a boy who has got the same mum and dad as you
words.ex: My sister is a girl, and my ___ is a boy.

words.def: a girl who has got the same mum and dad as you
words.ex: Mum and Dad have got two girls: me and my little ___.

words.def: your mum's mum or your dad's mum
words.ex: I call my ___ 'Grandma'. She makes very nice cakes.

words.def: your mum's dad or your dad's dad
words.ex: I call my ___ 'Grandpa'. He has got white hair.

words.def: a very young child who can't walk or talk yet
words.ex: My ___ sister is only three months old. She can't walk or talk.

words.def: your mum, dad, brothers, sisters and you
words.ex: I love my ___: Mum, Dad, my sister and me.

words.def: a person you like and play with
words.ex: Lucy is my best ___. We play in the park.

words.def: the special day each year when you get one year older
words.ex: Happy ___! You are eight today!

words.def: feeling good, with a big smile
words.ex: I'm ___ when I play with my friends.

words.def: with a lot of years; not young
words.ex: How ___ are you? I'm seven.

grammar.q: She ___ my big sister.
grammar.why: Use 'is' with he, she and it.

grammar.q: My grandma and grandpa ___ very kind.
grammar.why: Use 'are' for two or more people (they).

grammar.q: I ___ got two brothers.
grammar.why: Say 'I have got', but 'he has got' and 'she has got'.

grammar.q: My dad ___ got a big red car.
grammar.why: My dad = he. Use 'has got' with he, she and it.

grammar.q: ___ is that girl? She's my sister.
grammar.why: Use 'who' to ask about a person.

grammar.q: ___ old is your brother? He's ten.
grammar.why: Ask 'How old...?' to find out someone's age.

sentences: My grandmother has got white hair.
How old is your sister?
My baby sister is one year old.
Happy birthday to my mum!

reading.title: Meet Lily's family
reading.text: Hello! My name is Lily and I am eight. This is my family. My mother is a teacher and my father is a doctor. I have got one brother. His name is Max and he is five. We have got a grandmother too. She lives with us and she makes great cakes. We are a happy family!

units.title: Animals I know

words.def: a small pet with soft fur that likes to catch mice
words.ex: The ___ says 'miaow' and drinks milk.

words.def: a pet that says 'woof' and likes to run and play
words.ex: My ___ says 'woof' and runs after the ball.

words.def: a small animal that can fly and sing
words.ex: A little ___ is singing in the tree.

words.def: an animal that lives and swims in water
words.ex: A ___ can swim, but it can't walk or fly.

words.def: a big animal that people can ride
words.ex: I can ride a ___ on my grandpa's farm.

words.def: a bird that swims on water and says 'quack'
words.ex: The ___ is swimming on the water. Quack, quack!

words.def: a small green animal that jumps and lives near water
words.ex: A ___ is green and it can jump very well.

words.def: an animal with a long tail that lives in trees and likes bananas
words.ex: The ___ is eating a banana up in the tree.

words.def: a very big grey animal with big ears and a long nose
words.ex: An ___ is very big and grey.

words.def: a very tall animal with a long neck and long legs
words.ex: A ___ is so tall that it can eat from the top of a tree.

words.def: a long thin animal with no legs
words.ex: A ___ has got no legs, but it can move fast.

words.def: the long thin part at the end of a cat or a dog
words.ex: A dog moves its ___ when it is happy.

grammar.q: Can a bird fly? Yes, it ___.
grammar.why: Answer a 'Can...?' question with 'can': Yes, it can. Or: No, it can't.

grammar.q: A snake ___ walk. It has got no legs.
grammar.why: 'Can't' means it is not able to. A snake has no legs, so it can't walk.

grammar.q: I can see ___ elephant.
grammar.why: Use 'an' before words that start with a, e, i, o or u: an elephant.

grammar.q: Look! There's ___ duck on the water.
grammar.why: Use 'a' before most words, like 'a duck'. Use 'an' before a, e, i, o and u.

grammar.q: Grandma has got three ___.
grammar.why: For more than one, add -s: one cat, three cats.

grammar.q: Look at those two ___!
grammar.why: Some words change: one mouse, two mice.

sentences: The elephant has got big ears.
A frog can jump very well.
My cat has got a long tail.
The giraffe is very tall.

reading.title: At the zoo
reading.text: Today Sam is at the zoo with his dad. He can see two elephants. They are big and grey. A monkey is eating a banana in a tree. Sam likes the giraffes. They are very tall! There is a snake too, but Sam doesn't like it. It is long and green.

qs.q: How many elephants can Sam see?

units.title: Food I like

words.def: a round fruit that is red or green
words.ex: I eat an ___ every day. It is red and sweet.

words.def: a long yellow fruit that monkeys love
words.ex: This ___ is long and yellow.

words.def: a food that you use to make toast and sandwiches
words.ex: I put cheese on my ___ to make a sandwich.

words.def: a long orange vegetable that rabbits love
words.ex: This ___ is long and orange. My rabbit loves it!

words.def: long thin pieces of potato cooked in hot oil
words.ex: We have fish and ___ on Fridays.

words.def: a round white or brown food that a chicken gives us
words.ex: Let's cook an ___ for breakfast.

words.def: a sweet, very cold food that is nice on a hot day
words.ex: It is very hot. Let's eat a cold ___!

words.def: a drink made from fruit, like oranges or apples
words.ex: Can I have a glass of orange ___, please?

words.def: a white drink that comes from cows
words.ex: Cows give us white ___ to drink.

words.def: very small white food that you cook in water
words.ex: Mum cooks the ___ in water. It is small and white.

words.def: a soft, round red food that you eat in salads and on pizza
words.ex: I put a red ___ on my pizza.

words.def: the first food you eat in the morning
words.ex: I eat ___ at seven o'clock in the morning.

grammar.q: Can I have ___ apple, please?
grammar.why: 'Apple' starts with 'a', so use 'an': an apple.

grammar.q: There ___ two eggs on the table.
grammar.why: Use 'there are' for more than one thing: there are two eggs.

grammar.q: There ___ a cake in the kitchen.
grammar.why: Use 'there is' for one thing: there is a cake.

grammar.q: ___ is your favourite food? Pizza!
grammar.why: Use 'what' to ask about a thing.

grammar.q: We ___ got three bananas.
grammar.why: Use 'have got' with I, you, we and they.

grammar.q: ___ your milk, please.
grammar.why: To tell someone to do something, use the verb on its own: Drink your milk.

sentences: Can I have an apple, please?
My brother doesn't like carrots.
This ice cream is very cold.
What is your favourite food?

reading.title: Ben loves food
reading.text: My name is Ben and I love food! For breakfast I eat bread and an egg, and I drink orange juice. At lunch I eat chicken and rice. My favourite food is pizza with tomatoes. I don't like carrots, but my sister loves them. After dinner we have ice cream. Yum!

qs.q: What does Ben drink for breakfast?
When do they have ice cream?

units.title: My home

words.def: a building where a family lives
words.ex: We live in a big ___ with a red door.

words.def: the room where you cook food
words.ex: Mum is cooking dinner in the ___.

words.def: the room where you wash and have a bath
words.ex: I brush my teeth in the ___.

words.def: the room where you sleep
words.ex: I sleep in my ___. It has got a blue bed.

words.def: the place next to a house where flowers and trees grow
words.ex: We play football in the ___ behind our house.

words.def: you open it to go into a room or a house
words.ex: Please open the ___. I want to go into the garden.

words.def: a glass part in a wall that you can look out of
words.ex: I can see the garden from my bedroom ___.

words.def: a thing you sleep on at night
words.ex: It's nine o'clock. Time for ___!

words.def: a seat for one person, with four legs and a back
words.ex: Sit on this ___ at the table, please.

words.def: it has got four legs and a flat top, and you eat your dinner at it
words.ex: Put the plates on the ___ for dinner.

words.def: a long soft seat for two or three people
words.ex: We all sit on the big ___ and watch TV.

words.def: a piece of glass where you can see your face
words.ex: I look in the ___ and brush my hair.

grammar.q: There are three pictures ___ the wall.
grammar.why: Use 'on' when a thing touches the top or side of something: on the wall.

grammar.q: My shoes are ___ my bed, on the floor.
grammar.why: 'Under' means below something: the shoes are on the floor below the bed.

grammar.q: The sweets are ___ the box. Open it and take one!
grammar.why: 'In' means inside something. You open the box to get them.

grammar.q: There ___ three bedrooms in our house.
grammar.why: Use 'there are' for more than one thing.

grammar.q: ___ there a garden? Yes, there is.
grammar.why: Ask 'Is there...?' about one thing.

grammar.q: Please ___ the window. It's cold.
grammar.why: To tell someone to do something, use the verb on its own: close.

sentences: Our kitchen has got a big table.
The cat is sleeping on the sofa.
Don't open the kitchen window.
How many rooms are there in your house?

reading.title: My home
reading.text: This is my home. It is a small house with a big garden. There are two bedrooms. My bedroom is blue. My bed is next to the window. The kitchen is yellow and there is a big table in it. We have got a red sofa in the living room. My cat sleeps on it every day!

qs.q: The house has got a small garden.
The bed is next to the window.

units.title: Toys, colours and numbers

words.def: a round toy that you kick or throw
words.ex: Kick the ___ into the goal!

words.def: a toy that looks like a small person or a baby
words.ex: My sister's ___ has got long hair and a pink dress.

words.def: a toy that flies in the sky on a long string
words.ex: It's windy! Let's fly my ___ in the park.

words.def: a machine that can move and do things like a person
words.ex: My toy ___ can walk and talk!

words.def: a soft toy animal that children love to hug
words.ex: My soft brown ___ has got small round ears.

words.def: it goes on a railway and carries lots of people
words.ex: The toy ___ goes 'choo choo' around my room.

words.def: the colour of a strawberry
words.ex: Tomatoes and strawberries are ___.

words.def: the colour of the sky on a sunny day
words.ex: The sea is ___ and the grass is green.

words.def: the colour of grass and leaves
words.ex: Frogs and grass are ___.

words.def: the colour of bananas and the sun
words.ex: The sun is big, hot and ___.

words.def: a light red colour, like a pig
words.ex: Mix red and white paint and you get ___.

words.def: the number after nine
words.ex: Five and five make ___.

grammar.q: ___ is my kite, here in my hand.
grammar.why: Use 'this' for one thing near you.

grammar.q: ___ is my ball, over there in the garden.
grammar.why: Use 'that' for one thing far from you.

grammar.q: How ___ balls have you got?
grammar.why: Ask 'How many...?' to find out a number.

grammar.q: I have got two red ___.
grammar.why: Two is more than one, so add -s: two trains.

grammar.q: ___ is my teddy bear? It's under the bed.
grammar.why: Use 'where' to ask about a place.

grammar.q: These ___ my new toys.
grammar.why: 'These' means more than one thing, so use 'are'.

sentences: I have got a blue kite.
How many balls have you got?
Look at my new teddy bear!
My sister has got a pink doll.

reading.title: Kim's toy box
reading.text: Hi! I'm Kim. I have got a big toy box in my bedroom. In my toy box there are ten balls. Three are red and seven are blue. There is a green robot and a yellow train. My favourite toy is my teddy bear. He is brown and his name is Bobby.

qs.q: How many balls are in the toy box?
